main_body: A snow-covered log cabin: a large snow-covered roof slope (rows ~7-50) sitting above a dark wooden plank front wall (rows ~52-76) with a double arched door and two small windows.
top_band: Pale white/blue-grey snow roof slope, rows ~8-50 (a large foreshortened roof plane with a lighter eave edge at rows ~47-50), then the wall face below
evidence: Down the middle column: the roof surface is a large, clearly drawn snow slope with scalloped snow-clump shading (rows 8-46), then a bright front-edge snow lip (rows ~47-50), then a darker shaded strip with icicles (rows 51-54) that works as the eave shadow, then the vertical plank wall (rows 55-76) with a door and windows. The roof is a big visible top surface, like the reference houses. The door has dark iron bands and inset edges, and the windows have snow sills. Roof and wall are distinct, so it reads as 3/4 and not a front elevation.

style.evidence: The snow roof uses about 5 steps from white through pale blue to blue-grey, with clumped, scalloped snow texture and moss/dirt patches that match the tile-by-tile roof texture of the reference. The wood wall has plank grain in several browns, with dark brown outlines tinted toward the wood and a dark navy edge on the roof. Icicles, lit windows, wreaths and the iron door bands add varied detail. There are no large flat fills, and tile density is comparable to the reference. It would sit next to the Beodeul houses without looking thinner.
